original_question: If two Klein sails are not integer congruent, must their torus decompositions be different? Here a torus decomposition means the collection of integer-congruence types of the polyhedra in a fundamental domain together with their integer distances to the vertex of the cone.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 10 (V. Arnold) in §3.3, "Combinatorial structure of sails": "Torus decompositions of integer noncongruent Klein sails are distinct."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper's target statement very closely. It asks whether integer-noncongruent Klein sails are distinguished by their torus decompositions, and your gloss of "torus decomposition" is essentially the paper's own nearby wording: the collection of integer-congruence types of polyhedra in a fundamental domain together with their integer distances to the vertex of the cone. It also stays on the exact local problem in §3.3 rather than drifting to the broader neighboring realization problem (Problem 11) or the face-existence conjecture (Conjecture 12).
missing_details: The paper's torus decomposition is defined only for a periodic sail in the sense of Klein, so the question should explicitly restrict to periodic Klein sails.

The nearby context makes the periodic setting implicit via case [A]: algebraic cones, where a Dirichlet subgroup acts and the quotient sail is a torus. That algebraic/periodic setup should be stated if the question is to be fully stand-alone.
A fundamental domain should be understood as one for the relevant Dirichlet subgroup action on the periodic sail, not an arbitrary decomposition.
The phrase "integer congruent" should be made explicit as congruent under an affine transformation preserving the integer lattice, i.e. an element of the affine integer lattice group.
If one wants complete stand-alone wording, "Klein sail" should be anchored to the paper's notion of a Klein polyhedron/sail from Definition 2.4.

No extra polynomial-style parameters such as field characteristic, degree, homogeneity, nilpotency, or asymptotic quantifiers are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are geometric ones about periodicity, algebraic cones, and lattice-preserving congruence.
refined_question: Let S1 and S2 be periodic Klein sails arising from algebraic cones, so that each sail admits a fundamental domain under the action of its Dirichlet subgroup and the quotient is a torus. Is it true that if S1 and S2 are not integer congruent, meaning that no affine transformation preserving the integer lattice sends one sail to the other, then their torus decompositions are different? Here the torus decomposition of a periodic Klein sail means the collection of integer-congruence types of the polyhedra occurring in a fundamental domain, together with the integer distance of each such polyhedron from the vertex of the cone.
justification: The draft clearly targets the Arnold conjecture stated immediately after the paper's definition of torus decomposition in §3.3. The surrounding context there shows that the conjecture is about periodic Klein sails, and §3.1 explains the hidden reason a torus appears at all: in the algebraic case [A], the Dirichlet subgroup acts on the sail and the quotient is a torus. Definition 2.4 supplies the paper's notion of Klein polyhedron/sail, and Definition 1.1 supplies the congruence relation. So the draft is already very close to the paper-faithful formulation; the main refinement is to make the periodic/algebraic setting and the lattice-preserving meaning of congruence explicit, without broadening the problem beyond Conjecture 10.
